title: Two-state properties
objective: Encode conservation with primed variables, find the double-capture and buggy-refund witnesses, and fix each so that a witness you have not seen dies too.

choice.prompt: A capture is applied twice to the same hold. Which property catches that bug?

options.why: A double capture moves money. It does not create any {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture}}.

options.text: The merchant gains at most the hold's amount from it.
options.why: Two captures pay the merchant twice the hold, which breaks this property.

options.text: The held balance never goes below zero.
options.why: It catches the bug only when this hold is the only one in the pool. With other holds in `held`, it passes {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture}}.

blocks.md: A state is `(avail, held, merchant, status)`. A step is a relation between a state S and the next state S′, written with primed variables. A capture is `held′ = held − h`, `merchant′ = merchant + h` and `status′ = CAPTURED`. Two captures chain S → S′ → S″. Drawer D-04 holds the notation.

blocks.direction: Query asserts: with no guard at all, whatever leaves the sender arrives at the recipient. `prove` prints `proved` when no counterexample exists.

code.text:
from z3 import *
a, b, amount = Ints('a b amount')
a2, b2 = a - amount, b + amount     # the state after the step
prove(a2 + b2 == a + b)             # the total is conserved

options.why: Conservation needs no guard. The sender loses what the recipient gains {{run:RUN-z3-conservation-noguard}}.
Conservation is not non-negativity. "Money is safe" was never unpacked into one property.

blocks.after: Conservation holds with no guard {{run:RUN-z3-conservation-noguard}}. The model has two distinct accounts, so it cannot say what happens when they are the same one.

blocks.md: The buggy capture, applied twice to one hold, checked against five queries.
blocks.direction: Query asserts: for (i), two captures of one hold that change the total of `avail + held + merchant`. `sat` means such a pair exists.

code.text:
from z3 import *
Status, (HELD, CAPTURED) = EnumSort('Status', ['HELD', 'CAPTURED'])
h = Int('h')                                           # the hold's amount

class State:
    def __init__(self, tag):
        self.avail, self.held, self.merchant = Ints(f'avail{tag} held{tag} merchant{tag}')
        self.status = Const(f'status{tag}', Status)

S, S1, S2 = State(''), State('_p'), State('_pp')       # S, S', S''

def capture(x, y, guard=True):
    return And(guard, y.held == x.held - h, y.merchant == x.merchant + h,
               y.avail == x.avail, y.status == CAPTURED)

buggy   = lambda x, y: capture(x, y)                   # no guard
patched = lambda x, y: capture(x, y, x.held >= h)      # the pooled balance
fixed   = lambda x, y: capture(x, y, x.status == HELD) # the hold's own status

start = [S.avail >= 0, S.held >= 0, S.merchant >= 0, h > 0, S.held >= h, S.status == HELD]
twice = lambda step: [step(S, S1), step(S1, S2)]
total = lambda x: x.avail + x.held + x.merchant
gain = S2.merchant - S.merchant > h                    # the merchant gains more than the hold

def check(*formulas):
    s = Solver()
    s.add(*formulas)
    return s.check()

print(check(start + twice(buggy) + [total(S2) != total(S)]))   # (i) conservation fails
print(check(start + twice(buggy) + [gain]))                    # (ii) paid more than once
print(check(start + twice(patched) + [gain]))                  # (iii) the patch
print(check(start + twice(fixed) + [gain]))                    # (iv) the fixed capture
print(check(start + [fixed(S, S1)]))                           # (v) one capture works

options.why: The double capture lowers `held` as it raises `merchant`, so money moves, and the total is unchanged.
Each capture moves the hold from `held` to `merchant`, so the total never changes {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture}}.

blocks.after: Conservation holds even though the double capture is a bug {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture}}. It was the wrong property. (ii) asks for a merchant who gains more than the hold, and is `sat`: the merchant gains twice the hold. (iii) The patch "capture requires `held >= h`" reads the pooled balance. It stops the bug when this is the only hold, and fails when other holds share the pool, so it fixed the instance, not the class. (iv) Requiring `status = HELD` is `unsat`, and (v) one capture still works, so the fix is not empty {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture}}.

blocks.title: Twin: TigerBeetle
blocks.md: In TigerBeetle's two-phase transfers, a pending transfer "can be posted or voided only once", and a second post fails with `pending_transfer_already_posted` ("Resolve Funds" and "Errors", read 2026-10-23; pins in {{run:RUN-twin-pins}}). Which guard in your model plays the role of that error?

choice.prompt: The clamp refund rule credits the customer in full and floors the merchant at zero. A refund above the merchant's balance mints money, and the smallest witness is `c = 0, m = 0, r = 1` {{run:RUN-z3-refund-mint}}. Which fix also kills witnesses you have not seen?

options.text: Reject the refund when the merchant has nothing: `m = 0`.
options.why: `c = 0, m = 1, r = 2` still mints {{run:RUN-z3-refund-mint}}. This fixes the instance, not the class.
`c = 0, m = 0, r = 2` still mints {{run:RUN-z3-refund-mint}}. It kills the smallest witness and leaves a larger one.

options.text: Reject the refund when `r > m`, and debit exactly what you credit.
options.why: The mint query is `unsat`, and some refunds are still accepted, so the fix is not empty {{run:RUN-z3-refund-mint}}.

choice.prompt: A step takes state S to state S′. The property: "a refund never creates money", that is `total′ ≤ total`. Which formula do you hand the solver?

options.why: The negation of "total′ ≤ total" is "total′ > total", asked about a real step.
A model of this is a step that works, which says nothing about the others.
This searches for money destroyed, not created.
Any pair that is not a step satisfies an implication, so a model of it need not be a bug.

notes: Recorded by W1-T12. values.queries.<query> holds each query's verdict and rlimit; for a sat query, its witness (the primary configuration's model, as strings), the text of the primary configuration's replay (replay) and whether every configuration's model for it replayed (witness_replays); its unsat_core or minimum where it has one; the SHA-256 of its SMT-LIB export (null for the 2 queries without one: minimize_hold and minimize_pool_patched); and the verdict of each configuration that ran it (engines, cvc5's on the 10 queries it ran). Cite one as {{run:RUN-z3-double-capture#values.queries.<name>.verdict}}. 12 queries in all.

Where each configuration ran: native, pyodide-node, pyodide-chromium, pyodide-firefox, pyodide-webkit, cvc5-bench. native is the host under uv (CPython 3.13, the wheel z3_solver-5.3.1.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.whl from PyPI, no container); pyodide-node is Pyodide 314.0.7 with the z3_solver 5.3.1.0 pyemscripten wheel under Node 22 on the host (CPython 3.14 inside Pyodide); the pyodide-chromium, pyodide-firefox and pyodide-webkit configurations are the same engine in a module worker of each browser inside the pinned Playwright container (desktop builds, headless, not phones); cvc5-bench is cvc5 1.4.2, the Bench binary, in the Bench image with the network off.

Witnesses are recorded by property and never compared by value across engines [X RUN-z3-bv64-pyodide]: every sat query's model is replayed in plain Python integers by the script itself, in each configuration that gave one (native, pyodide-node, pyodide-chromium, pyodide-firefox and pyodide-webkit; cvc5-bench gives verdicts only), and the check is that every one of them replays. In this run the configurations in values.engines returned the same model for every sat query, which is a fact about this run and no promise.

Every query ran with rlimit 5000000 (spine section 9.1; values.queries.<query>.rlimit). The SMT-LIB exports are Z3's to_smt2() text with its let names (?x60, $x34) renamed in order of appearance, because Z3 names them after AST ids and the ids are not the same in every process: the raw text differed between Z3 configurations on 10 of the 10 queries that have an export (smt2_raw_sha256_by_engine). The renamed text is the same in every Z3 configuration, and its SHA-256 is values.queries.<query>.smt2_sha256 (null for minimize_hold and minimize_pool_patched, which have no export).

started_at and duration_s of a configuration that ran its own command (native, pyodide-node and cvc5-bench) are when that command started and how long it took, start-up included. Each browser configuration (pyodide-chromium, pyodide-firefox and pyodide-webkit) comes from one docker run, in which one browser session ran every Z3 script of runs/inputs/S1 in turn; that session is shared by the 9 Z3 records of runs/inputs/S1, and the configuration's argv and exit_code are its docker run's. A browser configuration's started_at is when its session began, after the browser had launched and before its page opened, and its duration_s is this script's own time in the worker, measured around the call without the engine's start-up and rounded to whole milliseconds by the harness. Its environment holds two spans that cover every script: session_wall_ms, from started_at to when the last script had finished (the page's and the engine's load and every script, not the browser's close), and docker_run_wall_ms, the docker run from docker_run_started_at, when the recording script started it, to its exit (adding the container's start and the launch of Node and the browser before started_at, and the browser's close and the output's chown after the last script). budget.harness_timeout_s is the wall time after which the recording script would have stopped a configuration's command (for a browser configuration, the docker run). The ms figure on an @@ line is the script's own measurement of that query's solver call, rounded to hundredths of a millisecond; in this record's browser logs pyodide-firefox and pyodide-webkit gave whole milliseconds, and pyodide-chromium gave multiples of 0.1 ms, on all 12 queries, so a browser figure of a few milliseconds is a rough one.

cvc5 1.4.2 [git 282d5e0 on branch HEAD] ran 10 of the 12 queries, each file under a 60 s limit (budget.per_file_timeout_s): every sat or unsat query that has an SMT-LIB export, as that text. The 2 Optimize answers have no export, and each is checked by a plain query that cvc5 ran and that asks for anything below the minimum (minimize_hold by no_smaller_hold, minimize_pool_patched by no_smaller_pool_patched). The checks require its verdict to equal Z3's on each one it ran (values.cvc5, and engines in each entry), and the plain query named for each query without an export to be unsat (checked_by in that query's check).

In native and pyodide-node, which ran on the host, argv's paths to the script are relative to a scratch folder that held copies of the configuration's inputs from runs/inputs/S1/RUN-z3-double-capture/ at the same relative paths, and the command ran in that folder; pyodide-node.mjs is named by its path from the repository root, and the <sandbox> paths are placeholders (next note).

Placeholders in argv: <sandbox>/engines is a scratch directory with Pyodide's npm package unpacked in pyodide/ and the Z3 wheel, both fetched and checked against their published digests (the inputs list them); <sandbox>/out is the browser container's output directory; <sandbox>/smt2 is a scratch copy of the SMT-LIB files the cvc5 configuration reads (the inputs list them). Repository paths are relative to the repository root.

Optimize (minimize_hold, minimize_pool_patched) answers are checked by a plain query that cvc5 also runs (no_smaller_hold, no_smaller_pool_patched), which asks for anything below the minimum: h < 1 and held < 2. Optimize has no SMT-LIB export, so smt2_sha256 is null for those two. no_smaller_hold is unsat by the premise h > 0 alone, h being an integer; no_smaller_pool_patched depends on the patch, which needs held >= h before each capture, so that held starts at 2h or more, which is at least 2.
